gd.plan.title: How to use TerraOrb Trip Planner
gd.plan.intro: This guide is for anyone planning a trip, a visit or an event in Sri Lanka. First, on Home, type a place and choose when you go, then press Check the weather. The other cards show what else the planner can do.
gd.plan.ask.name: Will it rain?
gd.plan.ask.what: Tell the planner where and when you are going. It says if the days look dry, maybe rainy or wet, names the best day, and shows a strip of days.
gd.plan.ask.step1: Open Home and type a place, for example Kandy. Choose it from the list that appears.
gd.plan.ask.step2: Choose When: Today, Tomorrow, This weekend, Next 7 days, or Choose dates.
gd.plan.ask.step3: Press Check the weather and read the answer and the Best day.
gd.plan.ask.step4: Tap a day in the strip to see it hour by hour, or press Save as a trip.
gd.plan.ask.tip: Rain by the hour comes from the Open-Meteo forecast, which is not NASA data. A forecast reaches only 16 days ahead and can change, so check again closer to the day. Days beyond that show only the usual pattern from NASA POWER, which is not a forecast.
gd.plan.explore.name: Explore places
gd.plan.explore.what: Search for a place or tap a dot on the map to see its weather for a day and the things that are good to do there in that weather.
gd.plan.explore.step1: Open Explore places and type a place name, for example Ella or Sigiriya.
gd.plan.explore.step2: Or tap a dot on the map, or choose a type such as Beach or Hills.
gd.plan.explore.step3: Choose a Day and read the weather and the list of good and not good things to do.
gd.plan.explore.step4: Press Add to my trip to save the place on a day.
gd.plan.explore.tip: The weather is the Open-Meteo forecast (not NASA data) for the next 16 days. A day further away shows only what usually happens around that date (NASA POWER), and opening hours are not known, so check them before you go.
gd.plan.trips.name: My trips
gd.plan.trips.what: Make a trip with days and activities, see the forecast for each activity, and let the weather check suggest moves. Nothing changes until you approve it.
gd.plan.trips.step1: Open My trips, type a Trip name, choose the First day and Last day, and press Create trip.
gd.plan.trips.step2: Open the trip and use Add an activity: choose the day, time of day, place and activity.
gd.plan.trips.step3: Press Check the weather. If there are problems, press Review changes.
gd.plan.trips.step4: Accept or reject each change, then press Save changes.
gd.plan.trips.tip: Trips are saved only in this browser on this device. Confirmed bookings are never changed, and activities beyond the forecast are not checked, because no forecast exists for them yet.
gd.plan.compare.name: Compare places
gd.plan.compare.what: Put 2 to 6 places side by side for the same dates, to see which one has less rain and a better score for outdoor plans.
gd.plan.compare.step1: Open Compare places and add 2 to 6 destinations with Add destination.
gd.plan.compare.step2: Choose the Start date and the End date.
gd.plan.compare.step3: Press Compare and read which place is marked Best.
gd.plan.compare.step4: Use Sort by to change the order, or Copy link to share to send it to someone.
gd.plan.compare.tip: Days up to 16 ahead use the Open-Meteo forecast (not NASA data). Later days use NASA POWER usual rain, drawn lighter, and have no temperature or score. The score is a planning guide, not a scientific index.
gd.plan.copilot.name: Ask the copilot
gd.plan.copilot.what: Type a question in your own words, such as which day is best for the beach. It answers from the weather data in the planner and says where the numbers come from.
gd.plan.copilot.step2: Type a question, for example Will it rain in Kandy tomorrow?, or tap one of the examples under Try asking.
gd.plan.copilot.step3: Press Ask and read the answer.
gd.plan.copilot.step4: Open Data and sources and How sure is this? to see where the numbers come from.
gd.plan.copilot.tip: The copilot is not a free-writing AI. It builds answers by simple rules from real data in your browser, and it says so when it cannot get the data. It never books anything and only proposes changes to your trips.
gd.plan.tools.name: Packing, calendar, settings
gd.plan.tools.what: Make a packing list from the weather and your activities, send a trip to your calendar as an .ics file, and change the limits used for alerts and scores.
gd.plan.tools.step1: Open Packing list, choose one of your trips and press Open packing list. Tick items as you pack, and add your own.
gd.plan.tools.step2: In My trips, open a trip and press Export to calendar (.ics) to save it to your calendar.
gd.plan.tools.step3: Open More, then Settings, to change rain, heat and wind limits and the score weights.
gd.plan.tools.step4: Press Save settings, or Back to standard values to undo your changes.
gd.plan.tools.tip: Settings, ticks and trips are saved only in this browser. A machine-learning estimate appears only if it beat the simple past-years baseline on data it had not seen, and hourly rain always comes from the Open-Meteo forecast, never from a model.
